content:
After adjusting its usage-based pricing structure in May, Google will soon impose limits on which Gemini models are accessible to free users and AI Plus subscribers.

According to a support document updated this week, users of the Gemini app who have not subscribed to Google AI will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From 9 October, users who do not pay for Gemini will no longer be able to access (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

On the other hand, AI Plus subscribers will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash; Pro will no longer be available. These users, who pay US$4.99 per month, will "receive an email explaining when the changes will take effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra are unaffected. Conversely, customers paying US$19.99 per month will be able to access the Deep Think option for "maximum parallel reasoning," a feature currently exclusive to the US$99.99 and US$199.99 monthly plans.

Gemini 3.1 Pro on AI Ultra, equipped with Deep Think

In October, the Gemini app also appears to be adding three computation intensity options — "low," "medium" and "high" — "available for every model that can be used."

At present, users can only activate the "Extended Thinking: complex problem-solving" feature. The three new computation intensity and thinking levels will align with the options available in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

It is still unclear how Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned. Google announced earlier this week that Argon will be offered first to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or as a new tier above Pro.
